The Strait of Hormuz is open again. Gulf oil is flowing at pre-war levels.

So why are Americans still paying around four dollars a gallon?

Gas is more than a dollar higher than a year ago.

Diesel is worse: up about two and a half dollars, after hitting an all-time record in September.

In California, diesel is around eight dollars a gallon.

Here's the catch: prices at the pump fall much slower than they rise.

Stations are still selling fuel they bought at higher prices. Tankers are paying for safer, costlier routes. And traders are pricing in the fear of new attacks.

In early October, crude was still about forty percent above where it was before the war.

The strait reopened. Your gas bill hasn't caught up yet. The American File.
titulo: Why is gas still $4 if the Strait of Hormuz reopened? #shorts
